subject: saturated correlates approach to missing data analysis

messages.author: 7c61453ccc67f9a0
messages.subject: saturated correlates approach to missing data analysis
parts:
Hi,
   I am trying to implement the SEM in the attached jpg.  It is taken from Craig Enders book "Applied Missing Data Analysis."  It is a simple regression model with the exception that two of the independent variables, referred to as auxiliary variables, are not used as predictors of the dependent variable, but rather as correlates of the residual on the dependent variable. The role of the auxiliary variables is to improve the estimation of standard errors given missing data and the fiml estimation procedure. There are 4 independent variables altogether, and they are all correlated with each other.  I have centered the two key predictor variables but not the auxiliary variables.  The model is saturated.  I get the following error statement:

Error in solve.default(E) : 
  Lapack routine dgesv: system is exactly singular: U[11,11] = 0
Warning message:
In estimateVCOV(lavaanModel, samplestats = lavaanSampleStats, options = lavaanOptions,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!


I have attached my syntax file and the text file with the data.  I would be very grateful for any help identifying
my mistake.

Thanks,
Bill Cook

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: saturated correlates approach to missing data analysis
parts:
Hi Bill,

What version of R and lavaan are you running?

sessionInfo()

I ran your code on R 2.15.3 with lavaan 0.5-12, and it ran without that warning (and SEs were provided in the summary). 

FYI, you don't need to manually specify variances of exogenous predictors in your script when you use the fixed.x = FALSE argument in sem(), and the estimator = "ML" argument is redundant when you specify missing = "fiml" (although I believe you can specify both if you wanted to use FIML with the robust estimator MLR).

Also, there is a function in the semTools package that automates the addition of auxiliary variables in your model so that you don't have to go through extra steps yourself.  You can just specify the simple regression in your script, then include a vector of auxiliary variable names in the call to auxiliary():

employ <- read.table("employee3.txt", header = FALSE)
names(employ) <-c("ID","age","tenure", "female", "well_being", "satisfaction",
                  "performance", "turnover", "IQ")
employ$well_being[employ$well_being == -99] <- NA
employ$satisfaction[employ$satisfaction == -99] <- NA

library(semTools)
?auxiliary

script <- 'performance ~ sat_c + wb_c'
mod1 <- auxiliary(script, data = employ, fun = "sem", aux = c("IQ", "turnover"))
summary(mod1)

You'll notice that the function will create single-indicator latent variables for the observed variables in order to accomplish the saturation of the correlates, but you can see that the corresponding estimates are the same as in the output from your manual model (once you get it to run, perhaps after updating your packages, or R itself).

Terry
